post.title: Meet Transcripts: Bot vs Meet API
post.hook: Two ways to get a Google Meet transcript, one view to compare them side by side.
post.summary: A Next.js app that fetches Google Meet transcripts through a self-hosted Attendee bot and through the Google Meet REST API, normalizing both into one shape. Setup scripts and a pinned Attendee checkout make it reproducible.
post.writeup:
## What it is
Meet Transcripts is a Next.js app that gets Google Meet transcripts two ways and shows them in the same view: a self-hosted Attendee bot, and Google's own Meet REST API. Both are converted to a shared `TranscriptLine` shape (`lib/transcript.ts`), so you can run both on one meeting and compare.

## Why
The two routes have opposite tradeoffs. The bot works on any Meet link and any account, runs live, but shows up as a participant someone must admit. The REST API is invisible and reads Meet's own transcript, but only for meetings you organized with transcription on, and entries are kept for 30 days.

## How it works
- **Bot:** `POST /api/v1/bots` with the Meet link, `meeting_closed_captions` for transcription and `recording_settings.format: "none"`, so no S3 bucket is needed. The `/bot/[id]` page re-renders every 3 seconds and reads the transcript endpoint until the bot reaches `ended`.
- **Google API:** list conference records, fetch transcripts and entries, then map participants to display names.
- **Setup:** `./attendee/setup.sh` clones Attendee at a pinned commit, builds one image, starts the stack, runs migrations and mints an API key into `.env.local`. It is safe to re-run.
- All Attendee and Google calls happen server-side, so no key reaches the browser.

## Findings
The first Attendee build takes 10 to 20 minutes and needs about 6 GB of Docker disk. The image is `linux/amd64`, so Apple Silicon runs it under emulation. Google tokens are stored in a local file, fine for one user only.

## Open questions
Captions are free but less accurate than a provider like Deepgram, which Attendee already supports. Webhooks could replace polling, and tokens need a per-user store before the app is shared.

slides.heading: The bot loop
slides.code:
1. POST /api/v1/bots with the Meet link,
   transcription_settings.meeting_closed_captions
   and recording_settings.format: "none"
2. The bot joins as a guest and waits in the lobby.
   Someone in the call admits it.
3. /bot/[id] re-renders every 3 seconds and reads
   GET /api/v1/bots/{id}/transcript
   until the bot reaches ended.
slides.caption: Nothing is recorded, so no S3 bucket is needed.
